Definition: glad tidings; by implication, reward for good news
BiblicalUsage: besorah covers good tidings, and it appears 6 times across the Bible. A runner brings good tidings to David, and the watchman on the wall knows good news by the way the runner runs.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that good news is meant to be carried, and the runner who brings it to David pictures every bearer of the gospel. That is why I keep coming back to it: besorah is not a word to rush past.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
